title: Split-stream attribution leak from partial-session resume during cross-deploy fallback
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: Several enterprise customers reported unexpectedly large invoices after a regional incident that triggered cross-deploy fallbacks (hosted -> dedicated or private). Investigation shows the spike was correlated with streaming requests that resumed partially after proxy reconnects; tokens from resumed segments were double-attributed into the hosted metering pipeline and again when the request landed on a dedicated/private runtime. This ticket tracks diagnosis, mitigation, and a full bugfix rollout.
repro_steps: 1) Simulate a long-lived streaming session through the edge proxy to hosted in region A. 2) Force a graceful fallback by bringing hosted routing policy down and route to a dedicated cluster in region B (simulated via route override headers). 3) During the handoff, interrupt the client so it reconnects and resumes using a resume-id; send the remaining stream chunks. 4) Observe metering pipeline: hosted ingest emits a partial-chunk usage event on disconnect; the reconnect emits resumed-chunk events which are not deduped against the original partial; the dedicated ingest also records the resumed chunks, resulting in ~2x attribution for the resumed portion.
observed_effects:
- Customer invoices inflated by up to 2x for affected streaming sessions.
- Customers: Nimbus Apps (10 tenants), ACME Health (1 enterprise account), internal demo tenant.
- Incident reports opened by SE and CSM teams; ACME Health marked as regulatory impact due to private deployment.
initial_hypothesis: Edge proxy emits an 'end-of-chunk' usage record when it loses the backend connection. The resumed session includes the same tokens because resume ID maps to the same logical request; downstream metering aggregator does not have a strong idempotency key across Hosted/Dedicated/Private ingestion paths, so resumed tokens are counted twice when the fallback causes a second ingest path to accept the data.
temporary_mitigations:
- Rolled out a rate-limited customer credit while we investigate (CSM actioned).
- Deployed an edge config change to delay emitting partial-chunk usage events for 10s after disconnect to reduce races (edge feature flag: chunk-grace-window).
- Manual backfill reconciliation script run for top 12 affected tenants (scripts in https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-scripts/pulls/214).
proposed_long_term_fixes: 1) Add a global dedupe key: combine tenant_id + session_resume_id + sequence_range to canonicalize streaming attribution across ingest paths. 2) Modify metering aggregator to treat overlapping sequence_ranges as idempotent across hosted/dedicated/private ingestion topics. 3) Extend ingestion contract to include 'session_origin' and 'last_seen_cluster' markers for cross-deploy routing to avoid double-emitting on handoff. 4) Add unit + integration tests that simulate proxy disconnect + resume scenarios across regions and deployment types.
implementation_plan:
- Spike (2d): design dedupe key format and perf implications (Liam, Priya).
- Spike result review (1d): Perf regression check on aggregator.
- Dev (5d): implement dedupe key in edge proxy and ingestion lambda; add aggregator idempotency layer.
- QA (2d): end-to-end with simulated fallback.
- Staged rollout: runtime-2.4.1 canary -> 25% -> 100% across hosted and dedicated pools. Private customers will receive a patch release and migration guide.
- Post-rollout: run reconciliation job and publish customer credits where necessary.
monitoring_and_alerting:
- New alert: streaming-attribution-dup-rate > 0.1% sustained for 15m.
- Dashboard: token-attribution-by-session_resume_id (linked) https://grafana.redwood.example/d/streaming-metering
- Weekly audit job to scan overlap windows and flag tenants for manual review.
communication:
- Notified CSMs and affected customers on 2026-03-02 with a temporary credit commitment.
- Public incident note drafted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/incident/ENG-80211-dedup-streaming.
- Postmortem to be published after rollout and reconciliation.
risk_and_rollbacks: Risk: dedupe layer could undercount if resume semantics change across older private deployments. Rollback: disable dedupe flag and fall back to delayed partial-chunk emission; run reconciliation to correct missed tokens if undercount seen.
